title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context: this is the part of 'Variations sur l'équation des lacets' where Grothendieck builds a Teichmüller-type group out of the profinite completion of the modular group. That group is generated by two torsion elements, ρ of order 6 and σ of order 4. On the previous page he expected the relevant group Γ_{ρ,σ} (or Γ̃_Q) to be close to commutative, with τ central. He now describes the group S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} concretely.

What the page does, step by step:

1. Set-up. Let 𝔖^{+∧} be a profinite completion of SL_2(Z) or GL_2(Z), possibly an orientation-extended version. Let M^![0] = Z^!_{ρ,σ} be a set of 'markings' u with two properties:
   - u carries σ to a conjugate of σ^{ε_2(u)};
   - u carries ρ to a conjugate of ρ^{ε_3(u)}.
   Let N^*_ρ and N^*_σ be the normalisers (in the ± sense) of ρ and σ. He claims a canonical homeomorphism
   M^![0] → Z_{ρ,σ} ×_γ N^*_ρ ×_γ N^*_σ.
   The right-hand side is the index-2 subgroup S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ} of S_0Γ_{ρ,σ}. It consists of triples (u, a, b) with u = f b = f' a for suitable f, f' ∈ 𝔖^{+∧}. Consequently ε_2(u) = ε_σ(b) and ε_3(u) = ε_ρ(a).
   A margin note records that S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ}/L_0 ≅ Γ̃_Q, the 'loop-equation' Galois-type group.

2. Formulas (49 bis). Writing out what u does to σ and ρ gives
   - u(σ) = int(f) int(b)(σ);
   - u(ρ) = int(f')(ρ^{ε_3}) = int(f' ε_3(τ'))(ρ).
   Here ε_3(τ') = τ'^{ν_3} when ε_3 = (−1)^{ν_3}, and τ' is a fixed element that inverts ρ by conjugation.

3. Solving for f and f'. Encode u by its conjugators α, β, as in his formula (38). Then:
   - int(f)(σ) = int(β)(σ) gives f ∈ β·C(σ) = β σ^i with i ∈ Z/4;
   - int(f' ε_3(τ'))(ρ) = int(α)(ρ) gives f' ε_3(τ') ∈ α·C(ρ) = α ρ^j with j ∈ Z/6.
   Both steps use that the centraliser of a torsion element in the profinite completion of SL_2(Z) = Z/4 *_{Z/2} Z/6 is the cyclic group it generates.

4. Proposition (50). The fibre of S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} over a fixed u is
   {(u, a = f'^{-1}u, b = f^{-1}u) : f' = α ρ^j ε_3(τ'), f = β σ^i}.
   It is a torsor under Z/4 × Z/6, the product of the two centralisers.

5. Next step. He picks the normalised element i = j = 0 as a set-theoretic section over u. On the next page he asks whether this section is multiplicative. He then characterises the section by congruences modulo Π̂_0 and starts, then crosses out, a corollary claiming the section is multiplicative.

Overall: routine fibre and centraliser bookkeeping, in service of comparing his group Γ̃_Q with a GT-like group of automorphisms of the profinite (1,1) modular group.
errors: In (49 bis), first line: the ε_2-twist is handled loosely. He writes int(f)int(b)(σ), which equals int(f)(σ^{ε_2}), as 'ε_2(u) int(f)(σ)'. In SL_2, σ and σ^{-1} are not conjugate, so an analogue of τ' for σ is implicitly needed or ignored. The likely reason it can be ignored is that the ambient group is GL_2-type or that one works modulo ±1. This is unclear rather than wrong.

Solving int(f)(σ) = int(β)(σ) as f = βσ^i needs the centraliser of σ (and of ρ) in the profinite group to be exactly ⟨σ⟩ ≅ Z/4 (and ⟨ρ⟩ ≅ Z/6). This holds in the profinite amalgam (Herfort–Ribes type results), but it is used without comment.

The 'homéomorphisme canonique' is written as if it were a group-like identification with a fibre product. The fibre product notation hides the γ_{ρ,σ}-compatibility conditions, which are only partly spelled out.

ideas.what: Describing the extended Teichmüller-type group S_0Γ_{ρ,σ} as triples (u, a, b): an automorphism or marking together with normaliser elements of the order-6 and order-4 torsion generators.
ideas.modern_name: Automorphisms of the profinite modular group preserving the conjugacy classes of torsion (inertia), as in GT and the (1,1) mapping class group
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme alludes to the 'Teichmüller tower' programme only in general terms

ideas.what: Fibre over u is a torsor under C(σ) × C(ρ) ≅ Z/4 × Z/6, using that centralisers of torsion elements in the profinite SL_2(Z) are the finite cyclic groups they generate.
ideas.modern_name: Centralisers of torsion in profinite free or amalgamated products

ideas.what: Normalised set-theoretic section (i = j = 0), and the question whether it is multiplicative, i.e. whether the extension splits canonically.
ideas.modern_name: Splitting / normalisation of a GT-type parametrisation (λ, f)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Drinfeld's normalisation of GT elements; Lochak–Schneps

deep.surprise_reason: This is careful but routine bookkeeping within Grothendieck's unpublished GT-type programme on the profinite modular group. The fibre computation follows directly from centraliser facts. It is mildly interesting as documentation of his independent 'loop-equation' approach to the Galois / Teichmüller group, but the page contains no result absent from the later literature.
transcription_corrections: 'M[0] ≃ 𝓜_{1,3}[0]' is likely 𝓜_{1,1}[0] or a tilde-variant; the orders 6 and 4 of ρ and σ point to the (1,1) / SL_2(Z) situation.
First line: 'Nous allons envoyer [?] dans la suite' is probably 'Nous allons essayer de sonder la suite' or similar; the text is illegible, uncertain.
Margin NB: reads roughly 'NB On a S_0Γ^!_{ρ,σ}/L_0 ≃(π) Γ̃_Q' and 'S_0Γ_{ρ,σ}/L_0^∞', followed by 'déf. γ_{ρ,σ}'.
The margin beside (50) reads 'où α, β, ε_2, ε_3, ρ^0, σ^0 définis par u (38)'.
In (49) the triple lies in Z^![0] × N^!_ρ × N^!_σ, as written under the braces.
